article.background: 达尔文晚年对自身认知能力、推理能力与审美变化的克制反思。只保留46-50五个划线目标句。

sentences.en: He believes that this very difficulty may have had the compensating advantage of forcing him to think long and intently about every sentence, and thus enabling him to detect errors in reasoning and in his own observations.
sentences.zh: 他认为，正是这种表达上的困难也许反而带来了一种补偿性的好处：它迫使自己长时间、专注地推敲每一个句子，从而使他能够发现推理中的错误以及自己观察中的偏差。

segments.text: He believes that this very difficulty may have had the compensating advantage of forcing him to think long and intently about every sentence, and thus enabling him to detect errors in reasoning and in his own observations.

sentences.en: He asserted, also, that his power to follow a long and purely abstract train of thought was very limited, for which reason he felt certain that he never could have succeeded with mathematics.
sentences.zh: 他还声称，自己沿着一条漫长而纯粹抽象的思路持续思考的能力十分有限，因此他确信自己绝不可能在数学上取得成功。

segments.text: He asserted, also, that his power to follow a long and purely abstract train of thought was very limited, for which reason he felt certain that he never could have succeeded with mathematics.

sentences.en: On the other hand, he did not accept as well founded the charge made by some of his critics that, while he was a good observer, he had no power of reasoning.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，对于一些批评者提出的指责——认为他虽然善于观察，却没有推理能力——他并不认为这种说法有充分根据。

segments.text: On the other hand, he did not accept as well founded the charge made by some of his critics that, while he was a good observer, he had no power of reasoning.

sentences.en: He adds humbly that perhaps he was ‘superior to the common run of men in noticing things which easily escape attention, and in observing them carefully.’
sentences.zh: 他谦逊地补充说，也许自己只是“比普通人更善于注意那些容易被忽略的事物，并对它们进行细致观察”。
